messages:
Liam O'Connor: Heads-up: Azure billed VAT on a marketplace invoice for ResellerUS even though their onboarding shows US tax residency. vendor taxed at EU rate $2,040.
Maya Singh: ouch. can you paste the invoice row?
Liam O'Connor: CSV excerpt: invoice_id,subscription_id,charge_type,amount,tax_rate,reseller_country
AZ-3041,az-sub-kk71,tax,2040,20,US
Liam O'Connor: reseller_country=US but vendor applied 20% EU VAT. ingestion shows reseller_tax_id present in our records.
Ben (finance): Do NOT pass tax through to reseller until cleared. post tax amount to clearing GL 3300. If Azure reissues refund we reverse.
TaxBot: Reminder: collect reseller VAT certificate or tax residency doc for vendor dispute. If unresolved >14 days escalate.
Maya Singh: opened Azure partner case #AZ-RES-7701 and attached reseller onboarding docs + invoice PDF. link: https://portal.azure.com/support/cases/7701
invoicing-bot: Automated: invoice AZ-3041 queued; flagged TAX-MISMATCH rule.
Ben (finance): action items: 1) Liam monitor Azure case and escalate in 48h (owner: Liam) 2) Finance hold tax pass-through and book clearing entry (owner: Ben) 3) Maya confirm we have reseller VAT docs stored in onboarding S3 (owner: Maya). Need VP signoff if we grant temporary credit >$1k.
Liam O'Connor: confirmed docs present in S3. will follow and ping legal if Azure refuses refund.
Maya Singh: i'll add ingestion alert for tax lines where reseller_country != tax_jurisdiction and missing matching tax_id: emit 'marketplace.tax_jurisdiction_mismatch'.
Ben (finance): acknowledged. looping in VP Finance for awareness. update thread when Azure responds. :thumbsup:
